The project supports the Government of Ethiopia to strengthen Human Resources for Health (HRH) systems, particularly in underserved and fragile settings where shortages of competent health workers, limited institutional capacity, and weak workforce information continue to affect access to quality primary health care. Through strong partnerships with government institutions, higher education institutions, professional associations, research institutions, and Primary Health Care Units (PHCUs), the project generates actionable evidence that strengthens workforce competency, institutional performance, service quality, and health system resilience. Working across all project objectives, the Advisor ensures that implementation is continuously informed by evidence through implementation science, operational research, program evaluation, learning agendas, adaptive management, and policy-oriented research. Ensure research activities directly support implementation, adaptive management, and policy development. Promote implementation science approaches that strengthen HRH systems and primary health care. Ensure alignment of research activities with Ethiopia's HRH Strategic and Investment Plan, national research priorities, and the America First Global Health Strategy. Coordinate ethical review submissions and regulatory approvals. Strengthen institutional research governance and ethical review systems. Support digitalization and modernization of Institutional Review Board processes where appropriate. Ensure scientific rigor, research integrity, and responsible conduct of research. Support development of innovative approaches for measuring workforce performance and institutional capacity.
